sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: China (Mainland) for WFOE registration; Taiwan as upstream investor jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Chinese mainland socialist legal system with regulatory hybridity for Taiwan-invested enterprises)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) between the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS), initialled June 29, 2010 and effective September 12, 2010

Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion between the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS), signed August 9, 2012 and effective February 1, 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation, Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (amended, effective January 1, 2025); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020); Law of the People's Republic of China on Protection of Investment by Taiwan Compatriots (2019 amendment); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised December 29, 2023, effective July 1, 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague route; Taiwan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, and no PRC consulate operates in Taiwan, so consular legalization is effected through cross-strait notarial verification: (1) obtain certified company registration extract from MOEA; (2) notarize before a Taiwan district court notary; (3) verify through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF); (4) verify through the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); (5) attach a sworn Chinese translation and submit to the local Administration for Market Regulation. Do not chain with any Hague Apostille step.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same cross-strait non-Hague route: notarize the MOEA-issued Certificate of Good Standing at a Taiwan district court, then SEF verification, then ARATS verification, then Chinese translation. Do not use Hague Apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the mainland China WFOE and UBO filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan investing company, authenticated by a Taiwan district court notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private-law instrument route: board resolution signed before a Taiwan notary, followed by SEF notarization verification and ARATS verification, then certified Chinese translation for submission to SAMR and the bank. No Hague Apostille is available or permitted for Taiwan-sourced documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) certified copy of company articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Non-Hague route using cross-strait verification: MOEA certified copy, Taiwan district court notarization, SEF verification, ARATS verification, Chinese translation, then submission with the WFOE incorporation application. This consular legalization-equivalent path is the exclusive route and must not be followed by any Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Taiwan bank for the investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan-based commercial bank maintaining the investor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter on official letterhead, bank seal certified by a Taiwan district court notary, then SEF verification, ARATS verification, and Chinese translation for presentation to the mainland account-opening bank. Taiwan being a non-Hague jurisdiction, no apostille may be applied; this is the sole consular legalization-equivalent path.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding the Taiwan parent and UBOs, apply layered screening at formation and continuously thereafter: (i) identify politically exposed persons (PEPs) among directors, shareholders, beneficial owners and close associates using World-Check, Dow Jones, or equivalent databases; (ii) screen against UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN/SSI/CAPTA, EU and HM Treasury sanctions, PBOC and MOFCOM unreliable entity lists, and domestic Chinese public security watchlists; (iii) investigate adverse media, shell-company indicators, and unexplained wealth; (iv) document source of funds and source of wealth for every UBO; (v) re-screen at least every 90 days and at any material event; (vi) retain all screening records for at least five years under PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration Online Service and the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) enterprise registration window at the planned WFOE registered address
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in simplified Chinese and must follow the statutory four-tier structure: Administrative Division + Trade Name (fanciful name) + Industry/Operating Characteristics + Organization Form. An English name may be adopted for banking and commercial purposes but cannot replace the Chinese registered name. The Taiwan investor's English name may be transliterated into pinyin to form a trade name only if the resulting trade name is at least two Chinese characters, is not misleading, and complies with local AMR review rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the SAMR system issues a written or electronic refusal notice with statutory reasons and a reference number. The applicant may (1) correct the name formulation and resubmit online, (2) file an administrative reconsideration with the next-higher Administration for Market Regulation or the same-level people's government within 60 days of receipt, or (3) after reconsideration, bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within 6 months. If the 30-day reservation expires, no automatic extension is available; a fresh name declaration must be submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by mainland Chinese tax authorities and banks for this industry. The State Taxation Administration expects a physical place of business for tax registration, invoice control, and records inspection, and banks under PBOC customer due diligence require an in-person interview, a valid lease contract, utility receipts, and frequently a site inspection. A registered address in a licensed free-trade-zone cluster address, government-supported e-commerce park, or business incubation center may be accepted if the enterprise has substantive personnel, books, and management presence there. A mere P.O. Box, mail-forwarding agency, or shared virtual office without a lawful sublease is likely to be rejected and will create a high shell-company red flag. For cosmetics DTC online retail, if inventory and operations are home-based, local policy must be checked; otherwise the WFOE should maintain a genuine service office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual unannounced inspection risk: 20-35% for a physical office with staff and complete books

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 1, 4, 98, 100, 101, 128, 192, 208, 277, 387, and 403; Regulations on Application for Company Registration (公司登記申請辦法); Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs; Central Region / Taipei City Business Registration Window; online via MOEA Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (公司設立登記申請書) together with Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) and the First Board of Directors Resolution (董事會決議錄).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan Company Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company conducting online retail of cosmetics. The subscribed capital must be reasonable relative to the stated business scope and paid into a newly opened NT$ bank escrow / capital verification account. A certified public accountant or certified public bookkeeper must issue a capital verification report (資本額查核報告書) stating that the capital has been fully paid before registration. The capital may not be withdrawn or loaned back to shareholders prior to registration except for permitted pre-incorporation expenses; such withdrawals may be deemed criminal misappropriation under Company Act Article 9.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2024-001 OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, TAIWAN. Adopted by unanimous written consent of the sole founding shareholder and the initial directors on [DATE], at [CITY], Taiwan, pursuant to Articles 192, 202, 208, 277 and 278 of the Taiwan Company Act. PRESENT: The undersigned shareholder appointed the following individuals to constitute the First Board of Directors: [Director A], [Director B], and [Director C], each of whom accepted office and confirmed their eligibility under Article 192 of the Company Act. CHAIRMAN: [Director A] was unanimously elected Chairman and Chief Executive Officer with authority to represent the Company and to execute all instruments and contracts necessary for the ordinary course of business. QUORUM AND WAIVER OF NOTICE: All directors waived formal notice of this meeting and agreed that the actions recorded herein constitute valid corporate action. RESOLVED, FIRST, that the Company’s registered office shall be established and maintained at [Registered Address], Taipei/Taichung/Kaohsiung, Taiwan, and that the Chairman is authorized to execute the lease, utility service agreements, and all filings with the Ministry of Economic Affairs to formally record such registered office. RESOLVED, SECOND, that the authorized share capital of the Company shall be NT$[AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] ordinary shares of par value NT$10 each, and that the issued and paid-up capital shall be NT$[AMOUNT], which amount is hereby declared to have been fully subscribed and paid by the sole shareholder. RESOLVED, THIRD, that all paid-in capital received from the shareholder shall be deposited in a dedicated corporate bank account opened for this purpose at [BANK NAME] and that such funds shall be held in escrow until completion of company registration; the Chairman and any one of the directors are hereby jointly authorized to open, operate, and execute related bank forms for such account. RESOLVED, FOURTH, that a corporate seal and a company chop shall be procured and affixed to all registration documents, contracts, and banking instruments, and that the Chairman shall maintain custody of the seals. RESOLVED, FIFTH, that [NAME A] is appointed General Manager, [NAME B] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME C] is appointed Compliance Officer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting; the CFO is authorized to prepare financial statements in accordance with IFRS and to file all tax declarations. RESOLVED, SIXTH, that independent accountants licensed in Taiwan shall be engaged to audit the capital verification report and annual accounts, and that the Company shall adopt internal control procedures sufficient to prevent money laundering in its cross-border direct-to-consumer beauty retail operations. RESOLVED, SEVENTH, that the Chairman, General Manager, and CFO, jointly or severally, are authorized to execute all registration forms, articles of incorporation, licenses, permits, e-commerce platform agreements, payment processor agreements, and any other documents required by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, tax authorities, or financial institutions. RESOLVED, EIGHTH, that this resolution shall be filed with the Company’s statutory records and, where required, attached to the incorporation filing. This resolution is effective immediately and may be relied upon by all governmental, banking, and commercial counterparties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Name and Trade Name Search System / Online One-Stop Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exhaustive name availability search on the MOEA Company Registration Search platform using three proposed English and three proposed Chinese company names. Each name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Taiwan company, must not contain prohibited words implying banking, insurance, or governmental sponsorship, and must include a designating term such as 'Limited', 'Co., Ltd.', or '有限公司' where required. Submit an online name pre-approval application using the founder's electronic certificate (自然人憑證) or the incorporation agent's digital certificate. If the applicants are foreign nationals, the application must include a notarized copy of the passport and a power of attorney. MOEA will issue a formal name reservation certificate valid for six months. In the event of rejection due to similarity, submit an amended application with fingerprint-clear alternatives within ten working days; administrative reconsideration is available by filing a petition with MOEA Commercial Administration Division within thirty days of the rejection notice.
required_dossiers: Passport or National ID of applicant shareholders
Power of attorney (if agent is engaged)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or placed in a pending nomenclature review, file a supplemental name application with at least three alternative names, or request a hearing before the MOEA Name Review Committee; the matter may be escalated to the Taipei High Administrative Court only after final agency denial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of constitutive documents, shareholder approval, and first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Taiwan (for foreign shareholder signatures) and the founding board; subsequently the same board will file with MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) in Mandarin with an English courtesy translation, containing the company name, registered address, business scope describing 'wholesale and retail of cosmetics, personal care products, beauty appliances, and related consulting services via the internet', share classes, director appointment mechanism, board quorum requirements, and fiscal year. Hold the constitutive shareholders meeting to approve the articles, elect at least one director (or three directors if a supervisory committee is adopted), and ratify the First Board Resolution participating in this dossier. All foreign shareholder signatures on the articles, board consent forms, and indemnity letters must be notarized at a Taiwan notary public or at a Taipei Economic and Cultural Office abroad, and, if executed outside Taiwan, legalized or apostilled by the competent authority of the country of execution. The board resolution must be typed in formal English and signed by all directors, with each signature witnessed and the resolution sequencially paginated. This package will later be converted into the statutory Chinese registration application by a licensed Taiwanese bookkeeper or CPA.
required_dossiers: Minutes or unanimous written consent of the constitutive shareholders meeting
First Board of Directors Resolution (English and Chinese translation)
Proof of registered office address (lease or letter of intent)
Power of attorney from foreign shareholder to local filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or MOEA returns the articles for amendment, obtain a supplemental board resolution approving the revised provisions and re-execute the pages requiring initialing; minor typographical errors may be corrected by filing an amendment resolution before registration is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital escrow deposit and CPA capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank (foreign currency or NT$ account) and a Taiwan-certified public accountant (CPA) registered with the MOEA and the Financial Supervisory Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital escrow bank account in the company's legal name at a Taiwan bank branch (e.g., Cathay United Bank, CTBC, or Taipei Fubon) using the company registration application and the foreign shareholder remittance authorization. Transfer the full paid-in capital from overseas in USD, CNY, or other convertible currency through proper cross-border remittance; the funds must be credited to the account and remain unrestricted except for the escrow restriction. Instruct a licensed Taiwan CPA to perform a capital verification by reviewing the bank passbook, exchange settlement certificate (foreign exchange receipt), remittance receipt, and shareholder subscription list, and to issue the capital verification report (資本額查核報告書) dated no earlier than fifteen days before filing. The CPA will also confirm the valuation of any non-cash assets if any, although for this DTC retail entity all capital must be cash. Once the CPA report is issued, the funds must not be disbursed until the MOEA registration certificate is obtained, except for statutory filing fees and pre-incorporation notarization costs which may be reimbursed from capital only with a supporting board resolution.
required_dossiers: Temporary bank escrow account opening form
First Board Resolution authorizing the bank account
Bank passbook or certificate of deposit showing cleared funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening due to compliance queries on beneficial ownership, resubmit the ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, corporate chart of the parent, and source-of-funds letters; if the CPA queries the foreign remittance currency source, provide a bank confirmation and purchase contract evidencing lawful conversion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company registration filing with MOEA and issuance of establishment certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs; registration filed through the Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop Electronic Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Company Registration Application System with an electronic certificate, or by presenting a paper filing at the MOEA Office, submit Form 1 (Company Establishment Registration) together with the verified Articles of Incorporation, shareholder consent, the First Board Resolution, director and supervisor consent letters, registered office proof, capital verification report, and payment of the NT$1,000 establishment fee plus NT$150 per each registration record. Ensure that all Chinese translations are certified and that all foreign signatures are matched with the same names on identification documents. The MOEA case officer will review the legality of the business scope, name reservation, director eligibility, and paid-in capital representation. Upon approval, MOEA will issue the establishment registration certificate, a unified business number (統一編號), and update the national company register. If the applicant fails to provide the bank account settlement for the capital, the application will be rejected. After approval, proceed to incorporate the company by applying for the company chop and corporate seal at a certified seal engraver, then opening the permanent corporate bank account and applying to the National Taxation Bureau for sales tax registration.
required_dossiers: Original signed Articles of Incorporation and translation
First Board Resolution and Chinese translation
Registered office lease agreement and landlord ID
Foreign shareholder identification and apostilled certificates
Power of attorney to local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a suspension or the registry queries the company name, director identity, or scope, respond within the given cure period (normally fifteen days) with a written explanation and supplementary documents; withdraw and resubmit the application if resubmission is faster, provided the name reservation remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory tax registration, VAT, and customs/import code enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of Taipei/Taichung/Kaohsiung (Ministry of Finance), and the Customs Administration of the Ministry of Finance if importing cosmetics
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the MOEA company certificate, apply online or in person at the local National Taxation Bureau for unified business tax registration (營業稅籍登記) using Form B (Start-up Sales and Business Tax Application). Receive the company tax ID number and registered taxpayer status. If sales will include physical cross-border or domestic retail of cosmetics where goods are imported to Taiwan, separately register as an importer with Customs Administration to acquire a customs registered importer number, and verify whether a Cosmetic Product Notification Filing (化粧品產品登錄) under Taiwan's Pharmaceutical Affairs Act is required for each branded product. For digital DTC retail, determine whether the primary sales host is outside Taiwan; nevertheless, Taiwan-incorporated company generally must include Taiwanese-sourced and all domestic sales in VAT filings. The National Taxation Bureau will schedule a VAT return and income tax registration, and will issue a Business Tax Certificate (營業稅務登記核定).
required_dossiers: First board resolution (for names and authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Taxation Bureau requests additional evidence of sales commencement or permanent establishment status, provide a board resolution declaring that operations will commence within six months and that the registered office is the administrative headquarters; if customs classification of beauty products requires an import license, coordinate with the Taiwan FDA (TFDA) before the customs registration will be finalized.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration (Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration (Taiwan) - Electronic portal: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a subsidiary in Taiwan, the entity must first complete company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA). After incorporation, the company must apply for a Business Tax Registration (統一編號) with the local National Taxation Administration. The application requires the company's incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, and identification of the responsible person. The Unified Business Number (UBN) is issued upon successful registration. For a foreign entity without a local subsidiary, a UBN may be obtained for VAT purposes if it has a fixed place of business or a permanent establishment in Taiwan.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$300,000 monthly sales (or NT$3,600,000 annual) for mandatory registration; however, for e-commerce, registration is required if there are sales to Taiwan consumers regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates electronic invoicing (e-invoice) for businesses with monthly sales exceeding NT$200,000. The e-invoice system requires real-time transmission to the Ministry of Finance's E-Invoice Platform (EIP) via API. For certain high-risk industries, anti-fraud digital stamping is mandatory. All e-invoices must be issued within 48 hours of the transaction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act. For goods, the goods must be physically exported from Taiwan. For services, the services must be provided to a foreign buyer and used outside Taiwan. For e-commerce, cross-border digital services provided to foreign consumers are zero-rated if the service is not used in Taiwan.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (外貨結售證明)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export zero-rating is claimed fraudulently or without proper documentation, the tax authority may impose a penalty of up to 5 times the tax amount, plus interest. Additionally, the zero-rating may be reversed and the tax assessed retroactively.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) – the statutory exchange control regulator; local SAFE branches supervise all onshore banking and cross-border transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, RMB is not freely convertible on the capital account, while current account transactions are generally convertible after banks verify authenticity and completeness. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) administers a strict registration, filing and use-control system. For a Taiwan-invested WFOE, inbound equity capital must first complete FDI foreign exchange registration with a designated domestic bank, after which the capital can be remitted into the WFOE's capital escrow account, converted to RMB via the bank, and used only for approved business purposes. Profit remittance to Taiwan is treated as a current account outward payment, but requires the WFOE to submit audited Chinese GAAP financial statements, finalised corporate income tax settlement certificates, a board resolution authorising the dividend, and evidence that no SAFE penalties are outstanding. The bank must verify that the paid-in capital has been capital-verified by a Chinese CPA and that the remittance does not constitute cross-border round

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Business Report (Company Act Article 20)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company and Commerce Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June following fiscal year-end (within 6 months of year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine NTD 10,000-NTD 100,000; continued default triggers daily fines and possible registration strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act Article 71)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May - 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers (custom year-end: within 5 months of year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to NTD 30,000 plus a 10% late-payment surcharge and interest; tax authority may conduct official assessment on default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to NTD 100,000; potential suspension of foreign investment privileges and future equity remittance applications.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Minute and Corporate Alteration Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company and Commerce Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of the resolution; for ordinary profit distribution at a June 30 AGM, no later than 15 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration makes the resolution non-opposable to bona fide third parties and attracts overdue-filing penalties (NTD 1,000 per item).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory CPA audit where paid-in capital exceeds NTD 30 million (approx. USD 1.0 million), or where the company satisfies two of three tests: NTD 30 million paid-in capital, NTD 50 million total revenue, 100 employees; otherwise audit is voluntary unless required by foreign parent or credit agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan GAAP (Business Entity Accounting Act) for non-public companies; public companies apply TIFRS/IFRS; international parents may require IFRS-consolidated schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing applies to private non-listed companies; share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members and, when the shareholding structure changes, the change is filed with the MOEA within 15 days. An annual internal UBO confirmation is recommended at the AGM and during the statutory audit.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 1,800 (NTD 28,000 - NTD 56,000) for local registered office/secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 5,000 (NTD 80,000 - NTD 160,000) for a digital retail WFOE with moderate revenue

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% under Article 4 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law (EIT Law), applicable to the WFOE as a PRC resident enterprise on worldwide income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Low-Profit Enterprise regime (EIT Law Art. 28): 20% statutory rate reduced further by a 75% income exemption, producing a 5% effective CIT rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million per annum, subject to employee headcount not exceeding 300 and total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million. No sector-specific tax holiday applies to online retail of cosmetics under ISIC 4791; the 15% High- and New-Technology Enterprise rate is generally unavailable to a pure online beauty retailer absent qualifying proprietary technology income. Foreign-invested WFOEs may access the Small Low-Profit preferential rate if all size tests are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual final settlement return: 中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类，2017年版，2021年修订）, main schedule Form A100000, filed exclusively via the State Taxation Administration e-Taxation platform (国家税务总局电子税务局, https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn), together with adjustment schedule A105000, foreign tax credit schedule A108000, and the related-party transaction annual reporting forms (G100000 series).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within five months after the calendar year-end, i.e., on or before 31 May of the following year. The WFOE is required to use the Gregorian calendar fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 / A100000 营业收入 (Operating Revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from DTC online cosmetics sales before deduction of platform commissions, payment gateway fees, shipping fees, returns, and discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offshore consolidated bookkeeping must map Shopify settlement reports and PayPal payout statements to PRC accounting records; total gross sales, not net remittances, are taxable revenue; foreign-currency receipts are converted at the PBOC central parity rate on the settlement date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 / A100000 营业成本 (Operating Cost)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and inventory movement for cosmetics inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inventory valuation must follow PRC Accounting Standards (ASBE); import duties and freight on bonded warehouse stock are capitalized into cost; write-downs require evidence of impairment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 / A100000 销售费用 (Selling Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Digital advertising, influencer marketing, marketplace commissions, and DTC customer-acquisition costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expense deductibility requires compliant invoices (fapiao); payments made for offshore services without PRC tax-paid proofs must be grossed up or added back; prepaid multi-year marketing contracts are capitalized and amortized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 / A100000 利润总额 (Total Accounting Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before income tax per PRC GAAP financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must agree to the audited stand-alone financial statements of the PRC WFOE; group consolidation entries at the Taiwan parent level are disregarded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 11 / A100000 纳税调整增加额 (Tax Add-Backs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenditures: excess entertainment expense above the 60% / 0.5% of revenue cap, non-fapiao expenses, administrative penalties, late surcharges, and disallowed related-party charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments proposed by the SAT examiner, including inflated royalties or management fees paid to the Taiwan shareholder, are voluntarily self-adjusted in this line to reduce penalty exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 14 / A100000 弥补以前年度亏损 (Loss Carryforward Utilization)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of unused tax losses brought forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PRC WFOE may carry losses forward a maximum of five years; losses cannot be carried back; the high-tech ten-year extension does not apply to a pure cosmetic retailer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 16 / A100000 税率 (Applicable Tax Rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% standard CIT rate; 20% for qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprises, yielding an effective 5% rate on the first RMB 3 million of taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The favorable rate is applied automatically upon meeting the three statutory size tests; misapplication is corrected retroactively with 0.05% daily late interest from the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 17-20 / A100000 应纳税额、减免税额、抵免税额 (Tax Payable, Reductions and Credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax, preferential deductions, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit is limited to the PRC quota computed on the same taxable income; Taiwan-source income subjected to tax in Taiwan under the Cross-Strait arrangement is credited through Schedule A108000, capped at the PRC CIT attributable amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 21-22 / A100000 已预缴所得税额及应补（退）税额 (Prepaid Tax and Balance Due)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly prepayments credited against the annual liability, with the final balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due after 31 May carries a statutory late surcharge of 0.05% per day; refund applications are subject to SAT desk review and set-off against other outstanding exposures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing carries an administrative fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid tax from the statutory due date; underpayment caused by concealment is penalized at 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Tax Administration Law Articles 62 and 63; intentional evasion in excess of RMB 50,000 and exceeding 10% of the payable tax is referred for criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201; failure to attach the related-party transaction schedules triggers a presumption of non-compliance and the special TP adjustment interest rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly prepayment return: 企业所得税预缴申报表（A类）, filed through the same STA e-Taxation portal with pre-populated data carried from the prior annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return and payment due within 15 days following each calendar quarter-end: 15 April, 15 July, 15 October, and 15 January for the fourth quarter of the preceding year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 / 按实际利润额预缴 (Prepayment Based on Actual Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative year-to-date actual accounting profit before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border settlement flows must be converted at the PBOC central parity rate on each settlement date; untranslated PayPal receivables cannot be deferred beyond the quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% standard rate; 20% reduced rate for qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprises within the RMB 3 million band.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Rate continuity must be monitored each quarter because breaching the size tests in a later quarter causes the annual settlement to recapture the full 25% rate on the entire year income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 / 本期应补（退）预缴所得税额 (Current Installment Payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Installment amount after crediting all prior quarterly prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Under-installment cannot be cured by an overpayment in a later quarter without interest consequences; a consistent under-withholding pattern attracts SAT monitoring flags.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment or late payment of quarterly installments triggers the 0.05% daily surcharge on the unpaid installment and automatic inclusion in the annual settlement adjustment; repeated delinquency blacklists the legal representative and may trigger exit-control measures before the annual return is filed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid by the PRC WFOE to non-resident shareholders under EIT Law Articles 3 and 37; reduced to 5% under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Arrangement (signed 25 August 2015, effective 8 February 2016) where the Taiwan-resident corporate shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividend and holds at least 25% of the paid-in capital of the WFOE.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Cross-Strait arrangement is administered as a de facto DTA. The Taiwan shareholder must: (1) obtain an annual Certificate of Residence (居住者證明) from the Taiwan competent tax authority; (2) deliver the certificate, a beneficial-ownership self-declaration, and evidence of the 25% ownership test to the WFOE as withholding agent before the dividend transfer; (3) repeat the certification for each calendar year in which dividends are declared; (4) prove genuine economic substance and business activity in Taiwan so that the reduced rate is not denied under the arrangement anti-abuse clause; (5) if the 5% rate was initially over-withheld, reclaim the differential through the PRC tax authority with the certificate attached. All documentation must be retained for 10 years by both the WFOE and the Taiwan shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT rates are 10% for both royalty and interest payments to non-residents. Under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Arrangement, the rates are capped at 7.5% for royalties and 7.5% for interest paid to a Taiwan-resident beneficial owner; treaty relief requires the same Certificate of Residence protocol and a showing that the Taiwan recipient is not a conduit.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (本地文档) is mandatory where annual related-party transactions exceed: RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for financial/financing transactions, or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions. Master File (主体文档) is mandatory where total annual related-party transactions reach RMB 1 billion. The annual related-party transaction report (年度关联业务往来报告表, G100000 series) must be filed whenever any related-party transaction exists, irrespective of these thresholds, under SAT Bulletin 2016 No. 42.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply UAE-style ESR but enforces a statutory substance-over-form doctrine through: (1) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under EIT Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulations Articles 120-122, which permits recharacterization of arrangements lacking reasonable commercial purpose and substance; (2) the beneficial-ownership test contained in SAT Bulletin 2017 No. 6, requiring the Taiwan dividend, interest, and royalty recipient to demonstrate real staff, premises, operational risk, and decision-making rather than conduit status; (3) the special tax adjustment regime with a six-year look-back and interest at the PBOC benchmark rate plus five percentage points; (4) deemed permanent establishment risk under the Cross-Strait arrangement because a Taiwan-parent online DTC operation run through a Chinese WFOE with sales fulfillment in China is treated as a China PE. The WFOE must employ substantive local management, warehouse/inventory risk, procurement contracts, HR, and independent bank accounts; absent such substance, profits are re-attributed to the Taiwan shareholder, the 5% WHT relief is denied, and the full 10% statutory rate applies with interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Underreporting of Online Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Shopify or PayPal settlement proceeds from the PRC books, diversion of sales revenue to offshore personal accounts, fabricated inventory shrinkage, or use of false fapiao to inflate operating costs of the cosmetics DTC business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax plus 0.05% daily late surcharge; confiscation of the evaded amount; aggravated tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 and representing over 10% of payable tax triggers criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201, with a fine and imprisonment of up to seven years imposed on the responsible person.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and actual controllers face joint and several civil restitution liability where corporate assets are stripped; SAT exit-control measures impose travel bans; personal bank accounts may be frozen under criminal asset-preservation procedures; the responsible director is subject to imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated royalties, management fees, or centralized procurement markups to the Taiwan shareholder or a Hong Kong conduit; persistent low margins or losses in the PRC WFOE while the Taiwan group earns the residual profit; failure to prepare or file the Local File and Master File at the statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SAT re-determines taxable income under EIT Law Article 41; additional CIT is assessed with interest computed at the PBOC benchmark rate plus five percentage points over the full adjustment period; fines of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 apply for non-production of contemporaneous documentation under Tax Administration Law Article 44; the special tax adjustment six-year limitation period applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve the transfer pricing policy are cross-examined in criminal tax referrals; exit bans and tax delinquency watchlisting are imposed on the legal representative; where funds were knowingly diverted out of the PRC, directors may be held jointly liable for the adjusted tax and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE or its Taiwan shareholder is a registered entity without staff, premises, operational risk, or banking substance, used solely to claim the 5% dividend WHT rate or to hoard arm's-length pricing benefits without any commercial foundation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization annuls the claimed tax benefit; the reduced 5% Cross-Strait dividend rate is denied and the full 10% WHT is re-collected with interest; related-party expenses are reversed into non-deductible items; the arrangement anti-abuse clause expressly authorizes denial of benefits for shell arrangements; retroactive adjustment up to ten years applies in cases of fraud or misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: PRC Company Law Article 20 veil-piercing applies where corporate personality is abused; directors are personally liable for company debts arising from the sham structure; foreign travel is restricted where flight risk is identified; criminal liability may attach for fraudulent use of the corporate form.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan shareholder provides related-party debt exceeding the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises, or accrues interest that is never paid in cash, or converts unpaid dividends into shareholder loans to strip profits without formal distribution resolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Interest on the excessive debt portion is non-deductible under EIT Implementation Regulations Article 119; the disallowed interest is recharacterized as a deemed dividend subject to 10% WHT (or 5% if treaty-qualified); consecutive-year violations attract a 50% underpayment penalty plus adjustment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who approve non-arm's-length shareholder loans face personal criminal exposure for failure to withhold the deemed dividend WHT; asset preservation orders may extend to personal holdings where the corporate form is abused to avoid tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Payment-Integrity and Cross-Border Information Exchange Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Layering of e-commerce settlement flows through unrelated third-party accounts, unexplained high-volume withdrawals, material mismatch between Shopify/PayPal gross sales and CIT/VAT returns, or false customs declarations on cross-border cosmetics shipments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law as revised in 2022, fines of up to RMB 5 million may be imposed on the entity; accounts are frozen; administrative blacklisting follows; profits traced to untaxed sources are confiscated in addition to the full back-tax and the 50% to 500% underpayment penalty; tax-relevant data is exchanged with Taiwan under the Cross-Strait arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge of the layering scheme face criminal liability for money laundering under Criminal Law Article 191, with imprisonment of up to ten years plus fines and personal asset confiscation; travel bans are issued, and cross-Strait mutual legal assistance enables extradition-style transfer for serious evasion cases.
